canonical_name: Kaplansky theorem on primitive PI algebras (candidate identity; exact formulation open)
statement_blocker: The catalogue gives only a broad PI-ring gloss and the year 1958. Kaplansky's inspected 1948 primary paper has a strong match in Theorem 1 (a primitive algebra satisfying a polynomial identity is finite-dimensional over its center), but it also contains other PI results and a distinct ring extension. Until independent review resolves the chronology, selects the intended theorem, and fixes algebra/ring, primitive-handedness, polynomial-identity, center, scalar, binder, and boundary conventions, choosing an exact proposition would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix the base field, associative/unital algebra or ring carrier, center carrier and scalar tower, faithful simple left/right module witness or equivalent primitive predicate, finite variable type, free noncommutative polynomial representation, and all universes and typeclasses.
conclusion: Candidate family only: a primitive algebra satisfying a nonzero polynomial identity is finite-dimensional over its center, or the paper's separately qualified ring extension. Exact root and encoding remain open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; zero/subsingleton carriers, empty variable type, zero or constant polynomial, missing faithful simple modules, center/base mismatch, algebra/ring coefficient conventions, and left/right primitive cases must all be resolved.
